business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electron Beam 3D Melting of Porous Titanium Hip Joint Prosthetics

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid (Civil Law for Quebec private law; Common Law for federal and public law)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Agreement Between Canada and the People's Republic of China for the Promotion and Reciprocal Protection of Investments (entered into force 1 October 2014)
Canada-China Income Tax Agreement (Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation and the Prevention of Fiscal Evasion with Respect to Taxes on Income, effective as of 1 January 1987)
United States-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) - Chapter 14 Investment (effective 1 July 2020)
Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA) - Chapter 8 Investment (provisionally applicable from 21 September 2017)
Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) - Chapter 9 Investment (in force for Canada since 30 December 2018)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17 (PCMLTFA) and its Regulations; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, s 462.3 et seq.; Special Economic Measures Act, SC 1992, c 17; United Nations Act, SC 1991, c 41; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 (individuals with significant control); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises of Quebec, CQLR c P-44.1, including requirements for ultimate beneficiary disclosure; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1; FINTRAC guidance under the PCMLTFA; Quebec Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the constitutional documents and proof of existence (certificate of incumbency or certificate of good standing) of each non-Quebec general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry of the foreign general partner's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille issued by the competent authority of the state of issuance; if not party to the Apostille Convention, consular legalization by the Canadian diplomatic/consular post of that state

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney or mandate from each general partner and beneficial owner authorizing a Quebec resident representative to file the declaration and receive service
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the foreign signatory's jurisdiction and, if applicable, a Quebec notary (notaire)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial certification, followed by Hague Apostille or consular legalization, and certified French translation if required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports or identity documents and proof of residential address for each authorized representative, director of the general partner, and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or government agency in the person's country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified notarial true-copy certificate, with Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus certified translation into French

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified source-of-funds statement or bank reference letter for each ultimate beneficial owner providing proof of the lawful origin of capital for the LP contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled/legalized bank certification and, where required, certified French translation; internal compliance file copy must also be preserved under PCMLTFA record-keeping rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Statutory declaration of the general partner confirming no PEP or sanctions-related prohibitions and no criminal record affecting fitness under Quebec public-probity standards
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Quebec notarial act; foreign notary acts require Hague Apostille or consular legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all ultimate beneficial owners, general partners, and authorized agents against (i) FINTRAC and OSFI PEP lists, (ii) Global Affairs Canada consolidated sanctions list issued under the Special Economic Measures Act and the United Nations Act, (iii) UN Security Council sanctions issued from time to time, (iv) OFAC SDN/50 percent rule where U.S.-dollar wire rails or correspondent banking are used, and (v) Canadian domestic sanctions regulations by country. The screening must be refreshed immediately upon any material change in control and at a minimum annually. Enhanced risk measures are mandatory for foreign PEPs, including source of wealth, source of funds, business rationale, and senior-management approval of the relationship, with contemporaneous documentation retained for at least five years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar) - Services du registraire des entreprises, online portal at https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11), a Quebec enterprise name must be in French unless an exception is recognized; limited partnerships must use the French legal designation 'société en commandite' or its abbreviation 'S.E.C.'; non-French names are allowed only if recognized and accompanied by a French version, and any transliteration must be in the Latin alphabet and free from characters or signs that would create ambiguity in the French-language register.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words that are identical or clearly confusing to existing names or trademarks in the Quebec enterprise register
Words implying an official status, public order, or professional medical competence where a license has not been issued
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If a name is rejected, the applicant must send a written request for review to the Registraire des entreprises within thirty (30) days of the notice of refusal, citing the reservation file number, the grounds for rejection, and any statutory basis for acceptance; the request can be amended to include two or three alternative names. The Registraire must answer in writing; if still refused, the applicant may contest the refusal before the Court of Québec (or the Federal Court if the issue arises under a federal name clearance) by filing a motion for declaratory relief within 30 days. Evidence of trademark availability and legalized translations should be attached; a healthy practice is to obtain a pre-clearance opinion from a Quebec trademark agent before amendment.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole place of commercial substance for an orthopedic-implant manufacturing entity. A physical Quebec workplace registered for the manufacturing activity must exist; the registered office may be an administrative or service address, but it cannot substitute for the production, sterilization, and quality-control facilities inspected by Health Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High - approximate risk of at least one unannounced Health Canada Good Manufacturing Practices inspection within the first 12 months of manufacturing operations is 70%; additional announced/unannounced visits by Revenu Québec, CNESST, and municipal zoning officers are probable if active production is declared.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name reservation request (single spelling/one French name) with Registraire des entreprises du Québec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff published by the Registraire; approximate market exchange rate used

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Declaration of establishment and registration of the société en commandite (limited partnership) at the Registraire des entreprises du Québec
AML/KYC screening database charges and enhanced due diligence on all ultimate beneficial owners (World-Check, UN/OFAC, PEP and domestic sanctions lists)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market subscription and per-report benchmark

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille/consular legalization and certified French translation of foreign corporate documents, passport copies, and bank letters
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary public, Global Affairs Canada/competent authentication office or consulate, and sworn translator in Quebec
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory fees for authentication plus prevailing notarial/translation tariffs; varies by document count

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Power of attorney and Quebec notarial acts for service of process and property authority
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Tariff of notarial acts (Quebec Notaries Act, tariff schedule) and market practice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal opinion on pre-incorporation matters, name clearance advice, registration drafting, and UBO register compliance
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Blended hourly or fixed arrangement at prevailing market rates for cross-border corporate setup

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Québec (CCQ), arts. 2236–2251 (limited partnership / société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 5, 14–20, 26–33 (registration and disclosure); where the general partner is a corporation, Québec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1 (governance).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) – Direction de l'immatriculation
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation d'une société en commandite (Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership) filed under s. 20 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital or escrow account requirement under Québec law. Each limited partner must contribute the amount or asset stated in the partnership contract (CCQ art. 2240); a limited partner who withdraws its contribution remains liable to third-party creditors for two years (CCQ art. 2250).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLUTION IN WRITING of the General Partner of The Titanium Implant Limited Partnership. Whereas the Partnership Agreement creates the partnership; and whereas the limited partners have subscribed to capital; IT IS HEREBY RESOLVED: (1) The capital subscription of each limited partner is confirmed and accepted, and contributions shall be credited to the partnership’s capital account. (2) The registered office is fixed at [street address], Quebec, Canada, in conformity with the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. (3) [Name] is appointed manager/officer of the general partner, with full authority to execute registration filings and declarations with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec and to open banking and funding arrangements for the partnership. Unanimously adopted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – online central registry name search service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a preliminary search of the REQ central registry to confirm the proposed limited partnership name is not identical to or confusingly similar to an existing enterprise. The name must include a legal suffix such as 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.' or 's.e.c.'. No formal name reservation exists for partnerships in Québec; compliance is verified by the registrar at filing, so legal counsel should obtain a written clearance opinion before execution of the partnership deed.
required_dossiers: Proposed partnership name and descriptive components
General partner's identification and NEQ number if already registered
Draft partnership agreement for name clause review
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the name as confusing, amend the distinctive element and re-file within 30 days of the notice; the applicant may also submit a formal name justification letter for registrar reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the limited partnership deed (contrat de société en commandite)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel in collaboration with a Québec notary (Chambre des notaires du Québec) where real property is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and sign the partnership contract specifying the firm name, head office address in Québec, identity of the general partner, each limited partner's contribution, profit-sharing ratios, management authority, and dissolution events. A private writing with witnesses is sufficient unless real property is contributed, in which case notarial execution is mandatory. Each partner must receive a signed counterpart.
required_dossiers: Full legal names and domiciles of all limited partners
General partner's registration extract or NEQ
Capital contribution schedule (cash, in-kind property, or services)
Head office address proof in Québec (lease or ownership title)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is defective, execute an amending agreement (acte modificatif); if a limited partner fails to make a promised contribution, the general partner may demand it judicially or seek dissolution under CCQ arts. 2240 and 2246.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the application for registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Services en ligne (online filing portal; paper submission at REQ counters also accepted)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and transmit the online 'Déclaration d'immatriculation – Société en commandite'. Enter the general partner and each limited partner's name, residential/registered address, contribution amounts, and the Québec head office address. The declaration must be signed electronically by the general partner or its duly authorized officer. Pay the CAD 39 (approx. USD 29) registration fee by credit card or Interac.
required_dossiers: Completed online registration declaration with electronic signature
Board resolution of the corporate general partner authorizing the filing
Copy of the partnership agreement (kept in the general partner's records; not filed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar issues a notice of deficiency under s. 31 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, correct and resubmit the declaration within the prescribed period; a refusal may be contested by judicial review before the Superior Court of Québec.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and publication of registration extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec – Publication and certification services
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance, the REQ assigns the nine-digit Québec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and issues the attestation of registration. The registration becomes public in the enterprise register. The general partner's counsel should download the official extract (extrait de registre) and verify that the legal form, head office address, general partner and limited partner disclosures are accurately published.
required_dossiers: REQ registration receipt and NEQ allocation
Official extract of the enterprise register
Internal copy of the partnership agreement (confidential, retained by general partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the published information is incorrect, file a voluntary declaration of modification (déclaration modificative) online within 30 days; failure to correct may render inaccurate publicity attributable to the partnership.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration provincial tax and municipal licence activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec; Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST); local municipality of the head office/facility
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Using the NEQ, open GST/QST, payroll and any sector-specific accounts with Revenu Québec; register the workplace establishment with CNESST for occupational health and safety; obtain the municipal general business licence (permis) and fire safety inspection before operations commence; present the REQ registration extract to the financial institution to open the partnership bank account and activate capital contributions.
required_dossiers: Proof of Québec head office address
Executed partnership deed and capital contribution evidence
Municipal zoning certificate and commercial lease
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec or the municipality contests the filing, cure the deficiency by submitting the missing supporting documents; municipal licence refusals may be appealed to the municipal permit appeals committee or Superior Court.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Directorate (federal MDEL) with provincial environmental oversight by the Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Establishment Licence (MDEL) under the Medical Devices Regulations (SOR/98-502); MELCCFP environmental authorization (certificat d'autorisation) under s. 22 of the Environment Quality Act, CQLR c. Q-2; municipal industrial occupancy permit

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP) – Direction de l'évaluation environnementale des projets industriels
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Registration/Declaration of Compliance (attestation de conformité) for a small- to medium-scale metal additive manufacturing facility; a full EIA report is not mandated unless annual output or emissions exceed the thresholds of the Regulation respecting the evaluation and examination of environmental impacts (RÉEIE).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: municipal sewer discharge must meet the Règlement sur l'assainissement des eaux usées municipales (≤15 mg/L BOD5, ≤15 mg/L TSS, pH 6.0–9.5, and titanium ≤1.0 mg/L per municipal bylaw). Air: Clean Air Regulation (Règlement sur l'assainissement de l'atmosphère) stack limits, including particulate matter ≤50 mg/m³, with filtration of inert-gas exhaust and metal fumes from electron-beam melting. Workplace: CNESST occupational exposure limits for titanium dust (TLV-TWA respirable fraction ~5 mg/m³). Waste: hazardous titanium powder manifests and tracking under the Regulation respecting hazardous materials, CQLR c. Q-2, r. 32.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Municipal fire safety permit and inspection covering electron-beam vacuum furnace hazards; structural load clearance signed by a licensed Québec Professional Engineer (OIQ) for 3D printers and vacuum chambers; CNESST workplace compliance clearance (machine guarding, respiratory protection, electrical safety); municipal building and occupancy permits with zoning conformity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal GST/HST and income tax accounts; Revenu Québec for Québec sales tax (QST) and provincial tax filings. Portals: CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) / My Business Account; Revenu Québec Online services (ClicSÉQ).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign limited partnership registers through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) to obtain a 9-digit Business Number (BN) with an RT program account for GST/HST; for QST registration, it files through Revenu Québec's CliCCh? CRA may require the non-resident partnership to designate a representative or agent in Canada. Revenu Québec subsequently issues the Québec enterprise number (NEQ) and QST registration; registration is effective as of the date the partnership first makes a taxable supply in Canada or Québec, whichever applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: A Canadian limited partnership is fiscally transparent for federal and provincial income tax purposes; it files a T5013 partnership information return and normally does not pay federal or Quebec income tax at entity level. Available elections include: (i) selection of a partnership fiscal period under paragraph 249.1(1)(b) of the Income Tax Act; (ii) GST/HST and QST election to have a one-time fiscal year change under section 241 of the Excise Tax Act with Quebec equivalent; (iii) elections under the anti-hybrid rules in section 20.2 of the Income Tax Act and the related amendments to hybrid mismatch arrangements; (iv) entity classification elections applicable only to certain trusts or partnerships for U.S. check-the-box purposes, not domestic Canadian elections.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST and QST (value-added tax; QST administered by Revenu Québec)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: $30,000 CAD (annual worldwide taxable supplies threshold for small supplier status under the Excise Tax Act and Quebec Sales Tax Act; once exceeded, the partnership must register for GST/HST and QST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance or digital stamping in Canada; electronic invoicing is voluntary, with open PEPPOL adoption. Revenu Québec may require XML invoices for certain registered suppliers, but for titanium orthopedic implant manufacturing there is no fiscal clearance API requirement. Businesses must retain electronic records and provide access to the CRA and Revenu Québec on demand.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: GST/HST and QST zero-rating applies to the supply of titanium orthopedic implants exported by the supplier or by the non-resident purchaser, provided the goods are shipped out of Canada, supported by adequate proof of export, and the supplier retains records showing the export occurred. The zero-rating eligiblity includes deliveries to a common carrier or courier for export, delivery to a freight forwarder for export, or direct export by the purchaser under a written contract stipulating export within 60 days. In the case of offshore services to non-residents (e.g., warranties, repair services) zero-rating may apply only where the service result is performed outside Canada or in furtherance of an export; all supporting documents must be maintained.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canadian Export Declaration (B13) filed under the Canada Customs Export Reporting System (CAED)
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical shipment to the non-resident
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank/heel? bank statement evidencing remittance of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The CRA and Revenu Québec may deny zero-rating and claw back input tax credits if insufficient proof of export is maintained; penalties include a $250 administrative penalty or 10% of the rebate claimed under section 285.1 of the Excise Tax Act for false statements, plus interest and late-payment penalties. Wilful attempts to evade tax or knowingly provide false information constitute criminal offences with fines of not less than 50% and up to 200% of the tax sought to be evaded and imprisonment up to five years. Revenu Québec imposes parallel penalties under the Tax Administration Act (Chapter 1, s. 31.5), including civil penalties for omission, negligent misstatements, or false declarations; assessments may be reopened within the normal four-year period, extended to seven years for misrepresentation and unlimited for fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) is the central monetary authority under the Bank of Canada Act; prudential regulation of banks and foreign-exchange operations is exercised by the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI); AML/ATF surveillance and cross-border wire reporting are administered by FINTRAC; export controls and sanctions enforcement are administered by Global Affairs Canada under the Export and Import Permits Act (EIPA) and the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA). Canada operates no separate foreign-exchange-control administration, no exchange-control law, and no surrender or conversion mandate for export receipts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the fiscal year of the limited partnership; must be filed every 12 months even during inactivity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of CAD 51 is applied, in addition to the regular CAD 34 fee; continued non-compliance for more than two consecutive years triggers administrative annulment of the partnership registration with the registering authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on the later of the partnership fiscal year-end and the filing deadline based on the fiscal period; for calendar year-end partnerships, the return must be filed no later than the last day of February (or March 31 for electronic filers), and T5013 slips must be distributed to partners by that same deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day, up to CAD 2,500, if filed beyond the deadline; additional penalties apply per partner for each month of delay in issuing T5013 slips, plus interest on any related income tax liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Medical Device Establishment Licence Renewal (health-regulated sector filing)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Health Canada – Medical Devices Bureau (regional notification)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on the anniversary of the original establishment licence issuance; renewal applications must be submitted at least 30 days prior to expiry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to renew results in immediate suspension of the establishment licence; continued operation without a valid licence may lead to Health Canada enforcement, including seizure, product detention, and prosecution under the Food and Drugs Act. No municipal recovery fee applies directly to the licence renewal unless provincial licensing permits apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Quebec limited partnership is not automatically subject to statutory audit solely because of its business type; an independent audit becomes mandatory if (a) the partnership agreement so requires, (b) the partnership is a reporting issuer under the Securities Act (Québec), or (c) the partnership is a collective investment vehicle falling under Chapter VII of the Securities Act. As an industry-standard commercial benchmark for a medical device manufacturing operation, a mandatory audit is typically expected by lenders, upper-tier investors, or contractual customers once annual gross revenue exceeds CAD 3 million, total assets exceed CAD 1 million, or the partnership holds a Health Canada Medical Device Establishment Licence for a Class III/IV device, such as a titanium orthopedic implant.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS as incorporated in the CPA Canada Handbook is mandatory for publicly accountable enterprises; for a private Quebec limited partnership, Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) is the applicable default framework unless the partnership is a reporting issuer or has voluntarily elected IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Quebec law does not impose a recurring annual UBO confirmation filing for limited partnerships. However, every modification affecting the limited partners, the general partner, their capital contributions, or the residence of a partner must be filed with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec within 30 days of the change. The Register of Limited Partners must be physically or electronically available in the partnership's establishment and updated continuously to reflect transfers, withdrawals, subscriptions, and assignments; annual confirmation is not required independently of the REQ annual declaration. For anti-money-laundering compliance under the FINTRAC regime, each partner's identity and ownership interest must be re-verified periodically and records retained for at least 5 years.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (member register with status of capital contributions)
Register of General Partner(s) and their management powers
Minute Book and Resolution Book (covering partner meetings and general-partner decisions)
Register of UBO identities for purposes of FINTRAC ongoing KYC obligations (if applicable)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 250 – CAD 1,500 per year (approximately USD 185 – USD 1,110) for commercial registered-office services or a corporate agent maintaining the enterprise registration in Quebec
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 15,000 – CAD 35,000 per year (approximately USD 11,000 – USD 26,000) for a certified independent audit of a manufacturing limited partnership with inventory, international trade flows, and substantial capital assets.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: Combined federal-plus-Quebec general corporate rate: 26.5% (federal Part I 15% + Quebec 11.5%); qualifying Manufacturing and Processing (M&P) profits: 24.5% (federal M&P rate 13% + Quebec general rate 11.5%). The Limited Partnership (LP) is fiscally transparent; Part I tax is levied on corporate partners at these rates on their allocated share of Canadian-source business income. Non-resident corporate partners are taxable on such allocations only where the partnership constitutes a permanent establishment (PE) of the partner under the applicable DTA.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Accelerated Capital Cost Allowance (CCA) for Class 43 (30% declining balance) and Class 53 (50% declining balance); 100% immediate expensing of eligible Canadian manufacturing and processing machinery and equipment acquired after November 20, 2018, with phase-out thresholds; federal Accelerated Investment Incentive (AII) providing up to 1.5x to 3x first-year CCA; Scientific Research and Experimental Development (SR&ED) investment tax credits (15% non-refundable, 35% refundable for CCPCs on the first CAD 3 million of qualified expenditures); Quebec SR&ED refundable credits (14% to 30%); Quebec additional deduction for eligible manufacturing equipment; regional tax holidays for Quebec-based 'e-business' or innovation-zone corporations.
